The Chukotka union is right in substance. The ~410 cells Cliopatria leaves out lie mostly east of 180 deg on the Chukchi Peninsula. It also added Wrangel Island, 24 cells with all their centres above 70.3 N, to Russia from 1778, and the Chukotka page says otherwise: 'In 1916, the Russians officially claimed the uninhabited island', which 'was subject to claims by the United States and Canada'. I made three changes. In ledger/26 (the 1778 gain) and the corrections of the 52 keyframes from 1778 to 1915, {region Chukotka} is now Chukotka minus the disc {lon -179.7, lat 71.2, km 90}, which resolves to exactly the 24 Wrangel cells. I inserted a 1916 gain of that disc from nobody (new ledger/136, before the dissolve, which is now ledger/137). The 1916 and 1917 keyframes keep the whole okrug. Re-validated: 0 errors, the same 5 warnings as before.
checks.fix: Wrangel Island (24 cells) removed from the 1778 gain and the 1778-1915 keyframes; a 1916 gain added (ledger/136).

checks.what: The pages support the cut: the purchase covered 'Montana, Wyoming, and Colorado east of the Continental Divide', and the Oregon Country was 'west of the Rocky Mountains'. The fixer's 12-point divide, however, ran straight from Rogers Pass (112.4 W, 47.0 N) to 111.4 W, 44.7 N. That put about 98 Montana cells of the Missouri headwaters on the Oregon side: the Big Hole, Beaverhead, Jefferson and Madison valleys around Dillon, Wisdom and Virginia City. Those cells were cut from the US for 1804-1819 and 1840-1845. The patches for 1820-1839 draw the divide correctly, so the dossier and patch years disagreed by about 100 cells. Lemhi Pass page: the pass 'lies on the Montana-Idaho border on the Continental Divide' (44 58 N, 113 26 W) and 'From the time of the Louisiana Purchase in 1803 until the Oregon Treaty in 1846' it 'marked the western border of the United States'. In all 20 places (ledger/24 and the keyframes 1805-1846) I replaced region A with two parts. Montana is now cut west of a new 12-point divide polygon: MacDonald Pass, Homestake and Deer Lodge passes, the Anaconda Range, Chief Joseph Pass, then the Idaho border. The patch p1820-p1839 polygons use the same points. Wyoming and Colorado keep the fixer's polygon. Region A falls from 969 to 871 cells, with nothing added. Dillon is kept American, while Missoula and Jackson (Wyoming) are still cut before 1846. I added a note on ledger/24 and the Lemhi Pass source. Re-validated: 0 errors, the same 7 warnings as before.
checks.fix: Region A (the land west of the Continental Divide) now follows the divide in south-west Montana, and the Missouri headwaters stay in the purchase.

Michigan page: '38,575 square miles (99,910 km2) of Great Lakes waters'; 'Michigan's western boundaries are almost entirely water boundaries'.

lydia_-550 is now the shape plus Ionia and Aeolis, which adds 32 cells (29 of them were in greek-city-states_-550). Ledger/13, ledger/14 and the successor land carry the coast on to Persia. Croesus page: 'Croesus annexed Ephesus into the Lydian Empire'; he attacked the coastal cities 'until he had subjugated all of mainland Ionia, Aeolis, and Doris'; with the islands 'he instead concluded treaties of friendship'. One minor point predates the fix: the gazetteer's Aeolis polygon takes in about 2 cells of eastern Lesbos (39.15 N 26.44 E and 39.3 N 26.35 E), although its own note says the islands are excluded. The greek-city-states handoff is correct.

New ledger/2 is a 1557 gain from habesh-eyalet over the sharifate's own 1201 Hejaz region. This matches the hierarchy.csv row (vassal of ottoman-empire, 1517-1802). Sharifate page: 'A dual system of government existed over Mecca'; 'Ottoman authority was only indirect, as the arrangement left real power with the Emir'. Habesh page: 'coastal Hejaz'; Burckhardt found the Jeddah pashalik 'reduced to perfect insignificance' by the Sharif. The 1865 keyframe of habesh-eyalet still takes the Hejaz back, as the fixer says (partly).
